data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Reliability gain is distinguished from mere compliance by the presence of 'Corrective Divergence' within the panel's internal deliberations.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The checklist is so explicit that no ambiguity exists to trigger divergence.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The panel is too intimidated to disagree, suppressing corrective divergence.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The 'Conflict-Resolution Mechanism': Mere compliance is characterized by uniform agreement with the checklist. A genuine reliability gain is evidenced when panel members disagree on a checklist item, engage in evidence-based deliberation, and arrive at the correct answer through the correction of an individual's error.
